news.headline: WTI Crude Oil Falls -0.78% to $81.59/bbl; Brent Also Drops
news.what_happened: WTI crude slipped from $82.23 to $81.59/bbl overnight as diplomatic progress on Middle East tensions reduced the geopolitical risk premium. Brent fell from $86.94 to $86.34/bbl.
news.why_it_matters: Direct cost relief for airlines (jet fuel 35-40% OPEX), paints (petroleum derivatives 40-50% input cost), tyres (synthetic rubber 60-70% input), logistics, auto OEM, and FMCG. OMC and upstream oil face margin pressure.

news.headline: Nvidia Bullish AI Earnings Outlook — Nasdaq Jumps +0.66%
news.what_happened: Nvidia delivered strong quarterly results with a bullish forward sales guidance, easing AI capex slowdown concerns. Nasdaq gained 171 points (+0.66%) to 26,151. S&P 500 +0.32%, Dow +0.30%.
news.why_it_matters: Nasdaq rally re-rates Indian IT stocks globally. With USD/INR at Rs 95.40 (structurally weak rupee), IT companies earn significantly more INR per dollar of US revenue. Nvidia's AI demand bullishness signals continued enterprise tech spend — core demand for TCS, INFY, HCLTech.

news.headline: Gold Surges +0.83% to $4,691/oz Near Record High
news.what_happened: Gold futures rose $38.40 to $4,691.70/oz, supported by strong safe-haven demand and central bank buying, even as US 10Y yields edged up to 4.664%.
news.why_it_matters: Higher gold prices increase collateral value for gold loan NBFCs — Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance benefit via lower LTV risk and ability to disburse larger loans. Gold at ATH triggers institutional re-rating of gold loan stocks.

news.headline: China Industrial Profits Slowest Growth This Year — Metals Headwind
news.what_happened: China's industrial profits rose only 11.2% in July, down from 15.1% in June — weakest pace of 2026. Industrial output rose 4.5%, missing estimates. Hang Seng fell 0.20%.
news.why_it_matters: China is the world's largest metals consumer. Slowing industrial activity signals weaker demand for steel, aluminum, and copper — near-term headwind for Indian metals producers with global exposure.

news.headline: RBI Shifts to Constant Rupee Intervention Strategy — USD/INR at 95.40
news.what_happened: Bloomberg reports RBI has moved to a more constant pattern of FX intervention to defend the rupee, backed by $73 billion of fresh dollar inflows since June. USD/INR flat at 95.40 today.
news.why_it_matters: Structurally weak rupee at 95.40 boosts INR earnings for IT and pharma exporters. RBI's active intervention limits further depreciation but signals underlying currency stress. Import-heavy sectors face structural cost pressure.
